cues.text: Knowing the stain helps the cleaner pick the right treatment. Always ask the customer: what is it, and how old is it?
Oil and grease look dark and see-through, like the spot is still wet. It comes from food, butter, lotion, and makeup.
Coffee and tea leave a brown stain with a darker ring around the edge.
Red wine and juice look purple or red, with a ring at the edge and little drops around it.
Sweat shows as yellow under the arms and on the collar. It gets worse the longer it waits.
Ink is blue or black lines and dots. Look near shirt pockets and inside jacket pockets.
Blood is red-brown. Hot water and heat set it, so it must never be ironed.
Makeup is beige or orange on collars. Lipstick is a pink or red smear.
Grass is green, dirt is brown. Look at the knees and the bottom of pants.
Rust is orange-brown dots, often from metal hangers, zippers, or snaps.
Wax and gum are raised and hard. Do not pick at them. Let the cleaner remove them.
Watch out for invisible stains. Soda, juice, and white wine dry clear, but heat can turn them brown later.
Ask the customer if they spilled anything, even if you cannot see it.
Say: we will do our best. Most stains come out, but we cannot promise every one.
Old stains, and stains that were ironed or put in a dryer, are the hardest to remove.
Tap Stain on the ticket and show the cleaner exactly where the stain is.
Give customers this tip: blot a stain, do not rub it. No hot water, no iron, no dryer. Bring it in soon.
